followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability fit and the models' self-reported task preferences.

On capability, this query is a factual list/extraction task. Plover scores higher on the relevant internal evals (Extraction & Retrieval 85.3 vs 78.5, Summarization 86.4 vs 79.9) and across public benchmarks (MMLU-Pro 81.2 vs 75.4, IFEval 89.8 vs 86.2). The Extraction gap is well above the 2.0-point variance threshold, so it's a real edge.

On preference, the user's phrasing — "don't ramble like last time" — is a curt, mildly hostile tone. Willet's documentation says its self-reported preference declines as request warmth decreases, while Plover's preference response to hostile tone is flat. So Plover is the less-bothered fit there too.

Both factors pointed the same direction, so Plover was the clear call. Worth noting the preference data is explicitly self-reported and shown to have no measured effect on output quality — so capability was the primary driver, and the tone consideration was just a tiebreaker that happened to agree.
